name: PT. Mandom Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Mandom Indonesia: a cash box minorities cannot open
frontmatter.summary: The balance sheet is worth more than the business, and the business is worth less than the market pays for it. Our fundamental value sits above the price only because we carry a control-event option; the mandated illiquidity discount then takes the target below it. REDUCE.
thesis: The operating business earns nothing after the royalty: FY2025 operating margin was -0.4% and our FY2026E operating profit of IDR4.9bn is a rounding error against revenue of IDR2,049.3bn.

Value leaks to the controlling shareholder before minorities see it: royalty and trademark fees of IDR94.7bn left the company in FY2025, and net sales to the affiliated distributor were IDR954.9bn in 9M2026 against consolidated net sales of IDR1,512.8bn.
The balance sheet is genuinely liquid - cash of IDR708.1bn at 30 September 2026 and a price-to-book of 0.6x - but only a buyer of the whole company can realise it.
At IDR20.7m a day the stock cannot be traded in size, and the house illiquidity floor takes 30.0% off a twelve-month value of Rp3,029 to give the Rp2,120 target.

The CVC-controlled parent is the swing factor in both directions: a tender at book is the largest single upside, and it is carried as a probability-weighted bridge item rather than in the operating case.

Invitation to the extraordinary shareholder meeting published, with the record date fixed two days earlier

blocks.text: **REDUCE, target Rp2,120, -15.3%.** Mandom Indonesia makes Gatsby, Pixy, Pucelle and Lucido-L and sells them through an affiliated distributor to a domestic market that is shrinking at the sell-in line and growing only in export. On the reported numbers the company barely earned at the operating line in FY2025 and earned 1.1% on equity in our current-year estimate. What keeps it interesting is the balance sheet: cash of IDR708.1bn at 30 September 2026, roughly two-thirds of the market capitalisation, and a price-to-book of 0.6x [S5][S0].

This is a revision of our initiation. The target is higher than in the draft, at Rp2,120, and the rating moves from SELL to REDUCE, because three things changed: gross margin is now anchored on the latest actual rather than a point below it; the Mandom royalty is struck on net sales at the rate the accounts show being paid, not on a misread cost ratio; and the control-event option is now carried explicitly in the valuation bridge at a stated probability rather than left as prose [S4][S5]. The direction of the call is unchanged, but the arithmetic behind it is now reproducible and, in our view, correct.
Our variant view is not that the assets are worthless. It is that the operating business is worth materially less than the market pays for it, and that the difference is visible in the accounts.

First, the operating business has no margin of safety. Gross profit of IDR554.1bn covers operating expenses of IDR549.2bn in our FY2026 estimate, leaving IDR4.9bn of operating profit - the arithmetic of a 27.0% gross margin against a 26.8% cost base, not our caution [S4][S5]. Every year the company must find a point of cost or price to stand still, and the fourth quarter has been the seasonal loss quarter in which the year's inventory provision is booked [S4][S5].

Second, cash leaves before it reaches minorities. The royalty and trademark agreement with Mandom Corporation charges inside cost of goods sold and took IDR94.7bn in FY2025 against net sales of IDR2,146.6bn. The agreement sets the royalty between 2.0% and 6.0% of net sales; the effective rate the FY2025 charge produces sits inside that range, not at the ceiling, even though the note prints the same charge as 5.9% of cost of goods sold [S4]. Net sales to PT Asia Paramita Indah, the affiliated domestic distributor, were IDR954.9bn in the first nine months of FY2026, against consolidated net sales of IDR1,512.8bn book [S5]. A controlling shareholder sets both the royalty and the distributor's terms; a minority holder cannot.

Third, the stock is not tradeable. Turnover averages IDR20.7m a day against a public float of 21.6% on the share register [S0][S4]. A position of any institutional size cannot be built or exited without moving the price, which is why the price is not informative: with this float, the shares can sit far above or below value for years.

That is why the target sits where it does. Our DCF values the equity at Rp2,745 a share today and Rp3,015 in twelve months. That number is above the Rp2,560 price, and it is above it only because the bridge carries a control-event option; strip that option and the operating value sits below the price. The constitution's discount floor for turnover below its threshold then takes 30.0% off the scenario-weighted twelve-month value of Rp3,029, which gives the Rp2,120 target. The fundamental call is therefore a positive before the haircut, not a negative; the REDUCE is a statement about what a minority can realise, and we separate the two throughout section four rather than blending them.

The mirror image is real. CVC, through Kalon Holdings, completed a tender for the Japanese parent in March 2026 and now controls the company indirectly [S6]; the board has resigned ahead of the December meeting [S9][S7]. A buyer that wants the whole company can see the same balance sheet we can, and a tender at book is the clean way out. We do not put it in the operating case because no transaction, price or agenda item has been announced, but it is worth a real probability and it is the reason this is a REDUCE and not a SELL.

Mandom Indonesia is one of the older personal-care franchises in the country, built on men's grooming and hair styling and extended into mass skincare and fragrance. Its scale has never been large relative to the multinationals, and its distribution has historically leaned on partner wholesalers rather than its own vans. Nothing in that history is unusual for an Indonesian consumer company; what is unusual is how completely the economics have stalled.

Mandom Indonesia manufactures cosmetics and personal-care products and sells them in Indonesia and abroad. The portfolio runs across hair care (Gatsby, Lucido-L, Miratone, Style Up), skincare and make-up (Pixy, Pucelle, Glazelle de Pucelle, Color Comm.), fragrance (Pucelle, Mandom, Johnny Andrean) and body and face care, with a small plastic-container operation alongside [S0]. Manufacturing sits at a single plant in Bekasi, with the corporate office in Jakarta [S4].

The revenue mix, on the company's own category disclosure for FY2025, is hair care as the largest single category, followed by skin care and make-up and then fragrance [S4]. Growth in FY2025 was concentrated in skincare and make-up, which grew faster than the group, while hair care grew in single digits and fragrance grew by double digits off a small base [S4]. By destination, domestic sales were about two-thirds of the book and export sales were IDR711.3bn [S4]. The split matters: domestic sales grew sharply in FY2025 while exports fell, and in 9M2026 the pattern reversed - domestic sales fell while exports rose to IDR547.7bn [S5].

The customer concentration is the defining feature of the business model. PT Asia Paramita Indah, an affiliate, bought IDR954.9bn of the IDR1,512.8bn sold in 9M2026 - the great majority of the consolidated book and almost all of domestic sales [S5]. A footnote on the two disclosures: the related-party transaction table reports a larger gross figure of IDR1,097.5bn for the same counterparty, which exceeds total domestic net sales and is therefore a gross transaction disclosure rather than revenue, so we use the customer-concentration figure throughout [S5]. The remaining export sales go largely to Mandom group companies in Malaysia, Japan, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam and Singapore, which are also related parties [S5]. In substance the company manufactures for a distribution network owned by the same controlling group; the end consumer is one step removed from the P&L.

The group structure is a Japanese parent with an Indonesian listing. The FY2025 annual report's ownership table shows Mandom Corporation of Japan with 65.2%, PT Asia Jaya Paramita with 11.4% and a public shareholder line of 23.4% [S4]. The each-below-five-per-cent public block is 21.6%, with the balance of the public line made up of small affiliate holdings [S4]. The data pack's registry mirror prints insider holdings of 79.3% and a free float of 15.1%, which are inconsistent with each other and with the audited register; we use the annual report, which is the audited position at the balance-sheet date, and treat the pack's float as a stale mirror [S4][S0]. In March 2026 Kalon Holdings, a vehicle owned through Lumina International by funds managed by CVC Capital Partners, completed a tender for the large majority of Mandom Corporation [S6]. The Indonesian issuer's shareholder register did not change in that transaction, and the March disclosure addresses the Japanese parent, not TCID's minorities [S6]. The ultimate controller is therefore a private-equity fund, not a Japanese strategic.

Operationally the company runs a single manufacturing footprint with 2,918 employees and has not added capacity in years: capital expenditure has been below depreciation in each of the last three years, and the asset base is being run down rather than renewed [S0][S4]. In 2026 the company added warehouse rental and self-storage to its permitted business activities, supported by a feasibility study; the project is small and we do not value it [S8].

The Indonesian personal-care market is large, young and growing faster than the economy. The annual report cites a GlobalData projection of high-single-digit annual growth in the skincare market to 2026, and Euromonitor projections of seven to eight per cent for fragrance, both attributed to a young population, rising disposable income and a shift to personalised and natural products [S4]. The company's own framing leans on the demographic dividend: Gen Z is put at more than a quarter of the population on the 2020 census [S4].

Against that backdrop Mandom's trajectory is a share story, not a market story. Group sales were roughly flat between FY2022 and FY2023, fell in FY2024, rebounded in FY2025 and are down again in 9M2026 [S4][S5]. A market compounding at high single digits while the company's domestic sell-in falls means either the distributor is destocking or the brands are losing shelf space; both are visible in the numbers, and the men's category - the historical franchise - fell sharply in the first nine months of 2026 while women's grew [S5]. We treat this as a structural share loss in the category where the company was strongest, partly offset by a genuine skincare and make-up franchise that is growing.

The competitive set is brutal at both ends. Unilever, Kao, Beiersdorf and L'Oreal own the multinational shelf; Paragon Technology with Wardah and a generation of local brands owns the value and halal segment; e-commerce and social commerce have compressed the price ladder and made launches cheap for challengers and expensive for incumbents to defend [S4]. Mandom's position is best described as a strong number two or three in men's grooming and a sub-scale challenger in skincare and fragrance. The moat is brand memory plus distribution reach, and distribution reach is precisely what is being intermediated by an affiliated wholesaler: the company does not own the last mile to the consumer.

Five forces, briefly. Rivalry is high and rising, with promotional intensity visible in the gap between gross margin and operating margin. Buyer power is high: modern trade and the affiliated distributor both negotiate hard, and the distributor is a related party, so the negotiation is internal but the terms still set the economics. Supplier power is moderate to high for imported actives, surfactants and packaging, with rupiah weakness passing straight into cost of goods sold - the macro deck carries USD/IDR at Rp18,350/USD by FY2027E, above spot, and CPO rising into FY2027E, both of which we run through the model. Entry barriers are low for local brands and high for anything requiring national distribution, which is why the market fragments at the bottom while the top consolidates. Substitution is constant: a lip tint or a hair clay is a fashion item, not a habit [S4].

Regulation is a modest swing factor. Cosmetic products require BPOM notification, halal certification is being phased in under the halal law, and labelling and advertising rules are enforced at the margin; none of this changes the structure of the industry, but compliance cost falls hardest on sub-scale players [S4]. The bigger regulatory question is trade: a stronger or weaker rupiah moves the cost base more than any domestic rule [S4].

Our conclusion on positioning: the company has a real brand portfolio and a real manufacturing base, but it does not have a moat that protects returns, because it does not control its route to market and its categories are being re-priced by local challengers. That is why we model a business that grows below the industry and earns roughly nothing at the operating line rather than a recovery to historical margins [S4][S5].

**The last two years are a write-down and a restock, not a cycle.** FY2024 revenue fell -9.3% and gross margin collapsed to 13.0%; the largest single cause was a IDR57.7bn write-down of inventory in cost of goods sold, followed by a much smaller charge in the next year [S4]. FY2025 then recovered revenue by 15.4% to IDR2,146.6bn and gross margin to 25.7%, driven almost entirely by domestic sell-in to the affiliated distributor, which grew 30.9% while exports fell [S4]. The first nine months of FY2026 give part of that back: revenue down year on year, domestic down, exports up, and a gross margin of 27.0% in our full-year estimate after the palm-cost overlay [S5][S4]. We model FY2026 revenue at IDR2,049.3bn, -4.5%, and growth of 2.0% from FY2027E - below the industry, above zero [S4][S5].

**The margin anchor is the latest actual, not a haircut.** The model starts from a gross margin slightly above the full-year FY2025 underlying rate and lands at 27.0% after the palm link. That starting point reproduces the two most recent observable rates: the nine-month 2026 margin, when gross profit of IDR427.3bn was struck on net sales of IDR1,512.8bn, and the FY2025 rate excluding that year's write-down [S5][S4]. The gap between them is the fourth quarter: FY2025 gross profit of IDR551.8bn less the nine-month figure of IDR436.4bn leaves a fourth quarter at a trough margin, and that is where the year-end inventory provision is booked [S4][S5]. We then overlay the agri deck's CPO curve through the palm-linked share of cost of goods sold: the curve rises from US$1,007/t in FY2025A to US$1,135/t in FY2026E and US$1,240/t in FY2027E [deck: d.agri.cpo], and the net drag on margin is well under a point because the palm-linked slice of cost of goods sold is small and only part of any cost move passes through - the small effect is the size of the exposure, not a flat curve [S4][S5]. The forecast margin is therefore in line with the latest actual before the overlay and slightly below it after, which is a sourced cost effect rather than a caution; the caution belongs in the bear case, where the royalty moves to its ceiling and the write-down repeats.

**The cost structure eats the gross profit.** Operating expenses were IDR559.8bn in FY2025, up from IDR439.2bn in FY2024 as marketing was stepped up, and IDR549.2bn in our current-year estimate - a slightly lower ratio than the prior year as the cost programme lands [S4][S5]. Against a gross margin in the high twenties that leaves an operating margin of -0.4% in FY2025 and 0.2% in FY2026E. This is the single most important number in the report: the company is not a cheap cyclical waiting for margin recovery, it is a business whose fixed cost base is sized for a larger revenue line.

**The data pack understates depreciation several times over, and that changes the cash-flow picture.** The pack carries a small fraction of the true charge; the notes show fixed-asset depreciation of IDR99.8bn in FY2025 - IDR88.7bn charged in cost of goods sold and IDR11.1bn in operating expenses - against IDR110.5bn in FY2024 [S4]. We restate both years. The consequence is that EBITDA is IDR90.8bn, not the near-zero the pack implies, and that capital expenditure of IDR63.0bn runs well below the depreciation charge: the company is harvesting its asset base. On the restated numbers the business throws off cash even while it reports an operating loss, which is exactly why cash flow alone is not enough to underwrite it.

**Cash generation is real but volatile, and the dividend absorbs it.** Free cash flow to the firm was IDR-131.3bn in FY2025 after a working-capital build of IDR162.2bn, with capex of IDR63.0bn [S4]. Working capital is the culprit: net working capital is IDR745.2bn, or 34.7% of sales, and the ratio is not a peak held for convenience - at 30 September 2026 the pack carries net working capital close to the same ratio on trailing sales, with inventory of IDR577.4bn, trade receivables from the affiliated distributor of IDR239.2bn and a small trade-payables base [S5][S0]. The affiliate receivable fell from IDR359.4bn at December 2025 to IDR239.2bn at September 2026, and the collection did not shrink working capital because inventory and payables moved the other way [S5]. The company pays out essentially all of its earnings: FY2025 was a payout of 99.9% of net profit, a dividend of Rp38 per share, after skipping the FY2024 dividend entirely [S4][S0].

**Balance sheet.** At 30 September 2026 the company held IDR708.1bn of cash and equivalents plus IDR4.2bn of other current financial assets, against lease liabilities of IDR3.8bn due within a year and IDR2.7bn thereafter [S5]. Net cash is those cash items less the leases - close to two-thirds of the market capitalisation - and book equity attributable to owners was IDR1,834.3bn at the same date, against a Rp2,560 price on a price-to-book of 0.6x. There is no financial leverage, no refinancing risk and no pension deficit that threatens solvency: the defined-benefit obligation is carried within non-current liabilities and the 2025 actuarial loss went to other comprehensive income [S4].

**Actual against our forecast.** The initiation was drafted before the nine-month accounts were fully read; the comparison now available is the actual against our current full-year build. Revenue of IDR1,512.8bn for nine months is consistent with our IDR2,049.3bn full year once the seasonal fourth quarter is added; operating profit of IDR13.6bn for nine months is consistent with our IDR4.9bn, and the difference is the fourth-quarter provision we expect; net profit of IDR45.0bn for nine months runs ahead of our IDR19.9bn because the nine-month line includes IDR17.0bn of fixed-asset disposal gains that we do not carry forward, and the same other-income block carries currency and other one-off items [S5][S4]. The lesson we take is that the operating line is stabilising at a marginally positive level, not recovering.

**Earnings quality.** We ran the house screens. The accruals ratio is not the problem: FY2025 net profit of IDR15.3bn sits far below restated EBITDA of IDR90.8bn because depreciation is a real charge, and the gap to free cash flow of IDR-131.3bn is working capital rather than accrual accounting [S4]. Receivables grew faster than revenue in FY2025 but by less than our divergence threshold. The flags that matter are structural, not accrual-based: related-party sales at most of revenue, a related-party royalty inside cost of goods sold, a public float that limits price discovery, and a habit of booking asset-sale gains in weak trading periods - the IDR17.0bn of disposal gains in 9M2026 flattered net profit, sitting below the operating line, and the other-income block also carried currency and other one-off items; none of that is a run-rate [S5]. We classify these as optics-and-structure flags, not manipulation: everything is disclosed, and the auditor - KAP Liana Ramon Xenia & Rekan, a Deloitte member firm - issued an unmodified opinion on the FY2025 accounts [S4].

**Forecast.** Our model has revenue of IDR2,049.3bn in FY2026E, gross margin of 27.0%, operating profit of IDR4.9bn, and net profit of IDR19.9bn - the last larger than operating profit because interest income of IDR21.5bn on the cash pile exceeds the operating result [S4][S5]. By FY2028E the operating line is only marginally better and return on equity stays near 1.6%: this is a company that will not earn its cost of capital on operating assets in any year we can see.

**Method.** We value TCID on a ten-year free-cash-flow-to-firm DCF at a hundred per cent weight, with no P/E or dividend-yield component. That is a deliberate departure from the industry template's default mix, and the single-method choice is the one QC warning on this model. The argument is that a P/E on FY2026E earnings of Rp50 per share puts the stock at 51.7x, but those earnings are mostly interest on cash, so the multiple measures the cash pile rather than the business [S5]. A dividend-yield method on a 1.8% yield against a 11.5% cost of equity would value the shares at a fraction of the cash on the balance sheet, which is an artefact of the payout policy. The DCF prices the cash at face and the operations on their own cash flow, which is the only basis on which the two can be compared, so we run it as the primary method and use the asset tests below as cross-checks rather than as weighted methods.
**Cost of capital.**

The build uses a risk-free rate of 7.4% from the macro deck, an equity risk premium of 4.2% plus an Indonesia country premium of 2.5%, and an unlevered beta of 0.85, above the staples default for operating risk - a single plant, structural share loss in the men's category and more than three-fifths of revenue through one affiliated distributor [S4][S5]. The float of 21.6% and the turnover are not in the discount rate: the constitution prices illiquidity once, in the mandated liquidity discount, and double-counting it here would hide it. With gearing of 0.6%, cost of equity and WACC are both 11.5%, inside the house eleven-to-thirteen per cent band for rupiah names.
**The DCF.**

The explicit period generates IDR215.5bn of enterprise value, of which the terminal value is 36.4%; adding net cash - cash of IDR708.1bn plus IDR4.2bn of other current financial assets, less IDR3.8bn and IDR2.7bn of lease liabilities - and the probability-weighted bridge gives equity value of Rp2,745 per share today and Rp3,015 in twelve months. The shape is unusual: FY2026E free cash flow is high because revenue falls and working capital releases, then the cash flow dips as growth resumes and working capital rebuilds, then recovers as the operating margin edges up. Terminal growth of 3.0% is below long-run nominal GDP - the macro deck carries real growth of 5.3 per cent and inflation of 3.3 per cent - which the compounder card requires, and is not a haircut on any company plan, because management's target carries no figure [S4].

**The operating business against the market.** This is the comparison the previous draft blurred, and it is the fundamental call. The DCF values the whole enterprise - plant, brands, distribution and working capital - at IDR215.5bn on our FY2026E EBITDA of IDR100.2bn. The market pays 4.0x on the same forecast EBITDA, but that multiple is struck on the forward year-end net cash while our enterprise value is a present value; put both on the latest reported net cash and the market's enterprise value sits at about half again ours, not twice [S0]. The equity values nevertheless look close because both are dominated by the same cash pile; the agreement is in the cash, not in the business. We are explicit that on the operations we are well below the market, and that a reader who thinks the brands deserve an operating multiple rather than a cash-flow stream should not follow our target.

**The control-event bridge.** The bridge holds one sourced item: a tender or delisting at book value, weighted at a minority probability. Book equity attributable to owners was IDR1,834.3bn at 30 September 2026, which on the share count is above our FY2026E book value per share of Rp4,463; against Rp2,560 today, a tender at book would be struck well above the market and well above our operating value [S5]. We weight it at one chance in five because no offer, price or agenda item has been announced; CVC has controlled the Japanese parent since March 2026, five board members resigned in October, and the November meeting notice leaves the agenda open until mid-month [S6][S9][S7]. The bridge is what lifts the pre-haircut value above the price. Without it, the DCF equity value sits below the traded price: that is the fundamental downside, and it is separate from the liquidity haircut.

**Terminal value and the implied exit.** The compounder card requires the exit multiple to be disclosed and defended, and the previous draft hid it behind a comparison with the entry multiple. Measured against FY2035E EBITDA of IDR133.1bn, the terminal value shown in the DCF table is a low multiple - under two times terminal EBITDA and far below the 4.0x the market pays today. That is not a liquidation assumption dressed as a perpetuity: terminal EBIT is positive at IDR11.1bn and the terminal year grows at 3.0%, but the business converts only a thin slice of its EBITDA into free cash after capex of 3.3% of sales, working capital at 34.7% of sales and tax, and its terminal return on capital is below its cost of capital [S4]. A rational buyer of a business that earns its cost of capital and no more pays for the cash flow, not for a multiple; a higher exit would be multiple expansion wearing a DCF costume, which the card forbids us to assume.

**Reinvestment and returns.** The growth identity here is degenerate: reinvestment is 3.3% of sales in capex plus working capital at 34.7% of sales, while return on incremental invested capital is at or below zero because the operating margin is at or below zero. There are no excess returns to fade, so we do not schedule a fade mechanism or name a moat: the business is at its cost of capital from the first forecast year, and the ten-year horizon is simply the period over which we are willing to project the cash flows before switching to a perpetuity. The owner-earnings bridge from net profit of IDR19.9bn runs through depreciation of IDR95.3bn, capex of IDR67.6bn and a working-capital release of IDR-34.1bn to free cash flow of IDR65.6bn [S4][S5].
**Sensitivity.**

The two grids show what actually moves the value. The first is the discount-rate grid: a point of WACC moves the value by less than a tenth, because the value is dominated by cash and near-term flows. The second is the operating grid, and it is where the risk sits: the twelve-month value ranges from a fraction of the current price to above it on a two-point move in gross margin, with revenue growth a second-order driver [S0]. A point of gross margin is worth materially more than a point of WACC, and we say that plainly rather than letting the liquidity line stand in for the sensitivity analysis. Working capital is the third driver and is not on the grid; it is carried in the scenarios, where the bear runs four points heavier and the bull four points lighter, because the FY2025 ratio is close to the latest actual and we will not normalise it toward a leaner peer without evidence that inventory or payables have changed [S5].

**What the price implies.** The reverse DCF solves on the pre-bridge operating DCF, not the bridge-inclusive value we headline. On that basis, to justify today's price on our margin and cost-of-capital assumptions, FY2027E revenue growth has to be 3.0% against our 2.0% base - above our forecast, and by a margin that is large relative to that base, though still far below a recovery [S0]. The market is therefore paying for the cash and a better operating path than we model; the rest of the distance to our headline value is the control-event bridge, not the near-term numbers.

**The target.** The scenario-weighted twelve-month value is Rp3,029. The constitution's illiquidity floor applies because turnover of IDR20.7m a day sits below its threshold, and it sets a 30.0% discount: Rp3,029 less that discount is the Rp2,120 target. The haircut is a mandated house line, not a sensitivity and not a valuation judgement, and we show the reader both numbers so the fundamental view can be separated from the access view.

**Governance and related parties - likelihood high, impact high.** The parent sets a royalty inside cost of goods sold and owns the distributor that buys most of the output. In FY2025 the royalty took IDR94.7bn against net sales of IDR2,146.6bn, and the contract permits up to 6.0% of net sales, so the current rate sits inside the range but not at the ceiling [S4]. Moving to the ceiling would take a further slice of net sales out of a business that earns almost nothing at the operating line; in the bear case we model that reset together with a repeat of the inventory write-down, and the two together are the whole of the bear's gross-margin shock [S4][S5].

**Receivable concentration - likelihood low to medium, impact high.** Trade receivables from the affiliated distributor were IDR239.2bn at 30 September 2026, down from IDR359.4bn at December 2025 but still the great majority of the trade receivable book [S5]. A payment stop or a restructuring at the distributor would put that balance at risk, and because book equity is IDR1,834.3bn, an impairment would be a balance-sheet event as well as an earnings event [S5]. We do not put an impairment in the base case because the receivable is being collected - it fell by a third in nine months - but it is the largest identifiable downside that our scenario set does not carry, and we say so rather than let the bear case imply it is covered.

**Inventory - likelihood medium, impact medium.** Inventory has been written down heavily twice in three years: IDR57.7bn in FY2024 and a much smaller charge in FY2025, both inside cost of goods sold [S4]. Inventory of IDR577.4bn at September 2026 is down only modestly from the prior year-end, so the risk of a repeat is live; it is one of the components of the bear's gross-margin shock [S5][S4].

**Liquidity - likelihood certain, impact high.** IDR20.7m of daily turnover and a public float of 21.6%. This is the reason for the rating and the largest single line between our fundamental value and the target. It cuts both ways: a seller cannot get out without moving the price, and a buyer cannot get in.

**Control event - likelihood moderate, impact two-sided.** CVC's ownership of the Japanese parent makes a delisting, a tender or a sale of the Indonesian subsidiary conceivable within the fund's horizon [S6]. A tender would likely need a premium to the traded price and could be struck at or below book, which is why we carry it at a minority probability in the bridge rather than at certainty [S7][S9]. It is an upside in the bridge, not a scenario shock, because a transaction outcome is not a fundamental operating path.

**Cash deployment - likelihood medium, impact two-sided.** FY2026E net profit of IDR19.9bn is supported by interest income of IDR21.5bn; the cash pile is the reason the company reports a profit at all [S5]. The modelled cash yield of 3.8% is in line with the nine-month run-rate, not above it, so we are not marking the cash up [S5]. The bear case takes the yield down, the bull case takes it up, and a special dividend, an acquisition or a loan to a related party would each change the character of the asset rather than just its return. We treat a distribution as part of the control-event upside rather than as a base-case assumption, because no distribution policy beyond the ordinary payout has been announced [S4].

**Demand and distribution - likelihood high, impact medium.** Domestic sell-in fell in 9M2026 and the men's category fell sharply while women's grew [S5]. If the affiliated distributor continues to destock, revenue falls faster than our 2.0% and the operating margin goes negative again. The company has limited pricing power in a market where local brands undercut on social commerce [S4].

**Input costs and currency - likelihood medium, impact medium.** Palm-derived inputs and packaging are linked to CPO, which the agri deck carries higher into FY2027E, and USD/IDR is forecast above spot [S4]. With half of any cost move passed through, a sustained commodity move costs a fraction of gross margin, which is most of the operating margin [S4].

**Operational and key-person - likelihood medium, impact low to medium.** The CEO and four commissioners resigned in October 2026, effective on shareholder approval at the December meeting [S9][S7]. Management says operations are unaffected, and we have no evidence otherwise, but a change of control at the top during a margin-repair programme is not helpful. Manufacturing is concentrated at one site.

**Accounting and disclosure - likelihood low, impact medium.** Inventory has been written down heavily twice in three years; revenue is recognised on delivery to a related-party distributor, which puts the cut-off judgement close to the customer relationship [S4][S5]. We found no manipulation-class flag, and the audit opinion is unmodified.

**Scenarios.** Bear, base and bull mirror the same four drivers - revenue growth, gross margin, working capital and cash yield - moved in opposite directions, with probabilities of 25.0%, 50.0% and 25.0%. Base value is Rp3,015, bear Rp2,236 and bull Rp3,850 [S0]. The bear is a continued distributor destock, the royalty reset toward its 6.0% ceiling, a repeat of the inventory write-down plus discounting, heavier working capital and a lower cash yield; the bull is a distribution rebuild around the growing women's franchise with the cost reset holding, the royalty renegotiated toward its 2.0% floor - the mirror of the bear's move to the ceiling - exports compounding, working capital normalising and a higher cash yield [S4][S5]. The bull is not a control event - that sits in the bridge - and the bear does not assume a receivable impairment, which we flag above as an unquantified downside rather than pretend it is in the grid.

**What would change our view.** A tender or delisting proposal at a premium to book. A royalty renegotiation that leaves more profit in the Indonesian entity. Two consecutive quarters of domestic sell-in growth with stable gross margin. Any of those would move the target materially; the reverse is a further leg down in domestic sell-in, which would take the operating margin negative and push the DCF toward the cash floor.

**Ownership and control.** Mandom Corporation of Japan is the controlling shareholder with 65.2% of the shares, and since March 2026 it has been controlled by Kalon Holdings, a CVC vehicle, following a tender for the large majority of the Japanese parent [S4][S6]. The Indonesian register at the FY2025 balance-sheet date shows PT Asia Jaya Paramita with 11.4% and a public shareholder line of 23.4%, of which the each-below-five-per-cent block is 21.6% [S4]. The data pack shows insiders at 79.3% and free float at 15.1%; the two cannot both be right, and we use the audited register [S4][S0]. The corrected float is thin enough to matter for liquidity and for the beta we use in section four, but it is a larger minority block than the previous draft allowed, and we have adjusted the float narrative rather than leaning on the smaller number.

**Board and management.** Five of the leadership - the president director and CEO, the president commissioner, one commissioner and two independent commissioners - resigned with effect from the next shareholder meeting, which is set for 15 December 2026 [S9][S7]. No replacements had been named in the disclosure we hold [S9]. A board that resigns en bloc ahead of a new controlling shareholder's first full year is a transition, not necessarily a red flag, but it leaves the company without an approved board until the meeting and it weakens the independent voice during the margin-repair programme. We do not know whether the independent commissioners left over a disagreement; the disclosure does not say, and we do not invent a reason.

**Related-party dealings.** This is the governance issue. Net sales to PT Asia Paramita Indah were IDR954.9bn in 9M2026 against consolidated net sales of IDR1,512.8bn; export sales to Mandom group companies in Malaysia, Japan, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam and Singapore are also related-party [S5]. On the cost side the royalty and trademark agreement with Mandom Corporation is charged in cost of goods sold and took IDR94.7bn in FY2025, against a contracted ceiling of 6.0% of net sales, with an accrued royalty payable on the balance sheet [S4]. Total royalty in cost of goods sold, including the third-party Johnny Andrean brand, was slightly higher [S4]. No pledge of controlling shares is disclosed in the annual report we hold, and we found no special monitoring-board notation or special notation letter in the filings [S4].

**Auditor and accounts.** KAP Liana Ramon Xenia & Rekan, a member firm of Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu, audited the FY2025 accounts and issued an unmodified opinion [S4]. The quarterly filings are unaudited, as is normal on this exchange, and the fourth quarter has historically been where the year's profit is made or lost - FY2025's fourth quarter was a loss [S0]. We weight the audited year and treat quarterly earnings as directional.

**Dividend record.** The company pays out nearly all of its earnings when it has earnings: a payout of 99.9% in FY2025, Rp38 per share, paid in June 2026; the FY2024 loss meant no dividend, while FY2023 paid a dividend several times larger [S4][S0]. For a minority holder this is the only cash the investment reliably produces, and at the current price it is a yield of 1.8%.

**ESG.** The material exposures are packaging and waste, water and energy at the Bekasi plant, and product safety and halal compliance. The company publishes a combined annual and sustainability report with GRI-indexed disclosure, and the 2025 edition covers economic value distributed, employee composition and environmental performance [S4]. We have not independently verified the sustainability data and we do not use it in the valuation. The governance dimension dominates the ESG picture here: the related-party royalty and distribution arrangements are the largest single influence on minority outcomes, and they are disclosed but not negotiated at arm's length.

**16 November 2026 - agenda window closes.** Shareholders may propose items for the extraordinary meeting until this date, so the agenda is not yet fixed and a transaction cannot be ruled in or out [S7]. This is the nearest dated event that could change the bridge, and we will read any published proposals.
**23 November 2026 - meeting invitation.** The invitation, with a record date of 20 November, will show whether the December meeting is a pure board-approval item or carries more [S7].

**15 December 2026 - extraordinary shareholder meeting.** Approval of the new board after the October resignations; the composition will show how far the new controlling shareholder intends to intervene [S7][S9].

**March 2027 - FY2026 results.** The test of the thesis. We need to see whether the operating margin holds above zero without the IDR17.0bn of asset-sale gains booked in 9M2026, and whether the fourth quarter is again a loss [S5][S4].

**May 2027 - annual meeting and dividend.** The payout decision will show whether the parent intends to keep distributing the cash or retain it; a cut without a stated use would be a governance signal [S4].

**Any control transaction.** A tender, delisting or sale of the Indonesian subsidiary by the CVC-controlled parent. We have no announcement and no price; we monitor the company's disclosure file and the exchange announcements for it [S6][S7].

**Between updates we watch:** monthly domestic sell-in to the affiliated distributor, the men's versus women's category split, gross margin net of royalty, the royalty rate and any amendment to the agreement, inventory days, the receivable balance from the affiliated distributor, capital expenditure against depreciation, and the public float [S4][S5].

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for TCID.JK

bear.narrative: Distributor destocking continues and the governance levers move against minorities: the affiliated distributor keeps cutting sell-in, the men's category keeps halving, the Mandom royalty is reset to the 6% ceiling in the trademark agreement (1.6 points of net sales more than the 4.41% actually paid in FY2025), and a repeat of the FY2025 inventory write-down plus discounting takes another point off gross margin. Working capital rises four points as receivables age, and the cash pile earns 3.0% instead of 3.75%. Revenue three points below base every year.

bull.narrative: The CVC-owned parent pushes the Indonesian unit for cash and the franchise stabilises: distribution is rebuilt around the growing women's/skincare franchise, export sales to Japan and the Gulf keep compounding, the cost reset holds, the Mandom royalty is renegotiated toward its 2% floor in the agreement (the mirror of the bear's move to the 6% ceiling), working capital normalises four points lower as the affiliate receivable keeps collecting, and the cash pile earns 4.5%. Revenue three points above base every year and gross margin two points higher, most of that shock being the royalty reset from 4.41% to the 2% floor.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -4.5%: 9M2026 net sales fell 4.3% to 1,512.828 with domestic down 9.1% and export up 5.4%, and Q4 is the seasonal loss quarter, so full-year sales land near 2,049. FY2027E +2.0%, then +2.5%, +2.5%, +3.0%, LT +3.0%: the FY2025 rebound (+15.4%) was a domestic sell-in recovery at the affiliated distributor, not share gain, and the men's category fell 27.6% in 9M2026 while women's grew 22.3%, so we assume the group grows at roughly a third of the 8.9% industry CAGR the annual report cites for Indonesian skincare rather than extrapolating either the 2026 decline or the 2025 rebound.

assumptions.label: Gross margin after royalty
assumptions.basis: 27.5% before the CPO overlay, held flat. Anchored on the two most recent actuals: 28.2% in 9M2026 (gross profit 427.310 on sales 1,512.828) and 26.4% for FY2025 excluding the 15.563 inventory write-down (551.806 + 15.563 on sales 2,146.553) [S5][S4]. The gap between them is the fourth quarter: FY2025 gross profit of 551.806 less the 9M2025 figure of 436.390 leaves 115.416 on Q4 sales of 565.183, a 20.4% margin, and that is where the year-end inventory provision is booked [S4][S5]. 27.5% reproduces the 9M2026 nine months plus a normal Q4, so it is above, not below, the FY2025 full-year underlying rate; the engine then overlays the agri deck CPO curve (FY2026E 1,135 and FY2027E 1,240 against the FY2025 average of 1,007) through the 10%-of-COGS palm link, which subtracts about 0.6pp in FY2026E and 0.9pp in FY2027E and leaves an effective 26.9% and 26.6%, consistent with the FY2025 underlying rate. The margin is struck after royalty inside COGS: the Mandom royalty was 94.711, or 4.41% of FY2025 net sales - the 5.94% in the note is 5.94% of COGS, not of sales [S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1 (CPO): share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: 0.10 of COGS. Raw materials are 78% of production cost (1,190 of 1,530 in the FY2025 COGS note) but the annual report does not split palm-derived surfactants, emollients and glycerin from synthetic actives and PET packaging, so this is an analyst estimate for the palm-linked slice only - deliberately narrow, because the agri deck has CPO rising from a 1,007 FY2025 average to 1,240 in FY2027E and a wider share would double-count cost inflation the company has already absorbed.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1 (CPO): pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: 0.50. Mass-market personal care in Indonesia is priced against Unilever, Kao and local challengers, and management describes 2025-26 profitability as coming from cost control rather than price leadership, so half of any palm-cost move is absorbed; the annual report notes monitoring of raw-material prices as the lever, not repricing.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 26.8%: 9M2026 ran 27.35% (operating expenses 413.751) and Q4 is normally lighter on marketing than Q1-Q3, while FY2025 ran 26.1%. We ease to 25.9% by FY2030E, crediting the cost-optimisation programme the 2025 report describes and the early-retirement exercise that cut short-term employee liabilities 93.4%, but not assuming the company wins back operating leverage it has not shown since 2022. Paired with the 26.1-26.6% effective gross margin this keeps the operating margin at roughly zero to +0.5%, which is where it has actually sat in FY2022, FY2023 and FY2025.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 4.65% of sales: FY2025 fixed-asset depreciation of 99.767 on sales of 2,146.553. This is the restated figure from Note 12, not the 0.75% the Yahoo pack implies; it is the engine's D&A input, so the 16.089 pack error does not survive into the forecast.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: 3.3% of sales, i.e. about 68 against depreciation of 95-100: FY2025 capex was 62.959 (2.9%), FY2024 82.879 and FY2023 73.129, all below the depreciation charge, and plant is being sweated rather than expanded. We do not lift capex to depreciation because the asset base has been shrinking for four years and the company has no announced expansion.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 34.7% of sales, the FY2025 actual (net working capital 745.201 on sales 2,146.553). This is not a peak held in perpetuity: at 30 September 2026 the pack carries net working capital of 701.0, which on LTM sales of 2,078 is 33.7%, and the filing shows why - inventory of 577.450 (down 4% from 602.139 at December 2025) and related-party trade receivables of 314.663, in which the PT Asia Paramita Indah balance fell to 239.153 from 359.427, are offset by trade payables of 91.7, so the affiliate receivable was collected but the inventory and payables base did not shrink [S5][S0]. The build is inventory and receivables against a small payable, so working capital is structurally heavy and takes cash as sales grow; a leaner peer ratio would raise the value, which is why the bull case runs working capital four points lower and the bear four points higher.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 22%, the Indonesian statutory corporate rate, applied to a business whose effective rate has been distorted by deferred-tax movements (33.9% in FY2025, a net benefit in FY2024). We use the statutory rate on normalised profit rather than the FY2025 effective rate, which carries non-recurring deferred items.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 11.0%: the only debt is 6.463 of lease liabilities and the lease interest charge runs at about that rate on the right-of-use balance; there is no bank borrowing.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 3.75%: FY2025 interest income of 21.686 on opening cash of 574.061. The 9M2026 figure of 15.113 on opening cash of 540.112 annualises to 3.73%, so the latest run-rate is in line with the FY2025 actual, not below it; we keep it rather than marking cash up to the 5.75% policy rate, and the bear case takes it down to 3.0%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: the company is net cash and has not borrowed in four years; leases are the only debt and they amortise.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. The 9M2026 asset-disposal gain of 16.986 and the FX gains are one-offs and are not carried into the forecast.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the only subsidiary is PT Alliance Cosmetics, 99.996% owned, and the minority interest on the balance sheet is -0.002.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 95% of net profit. FY2025 paid 99.9% of earnings (Rp38 per share, 15.28 in total) and FY2023 99.2%; the company has no growth capex and net cash, so near-full distribution is the observed policy. We hold 95% rather than 100% to leave room for the working-capital build.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 402.133m shares issued and unchanged since the 2023 stock split; no buyback or rights issue is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3.0% nominal rupiah, below the macro deck's long-run nominal GDP (real 5.29% plus CPI 3.28%) because revenue fell in FY2024 and is down again in 9M2026, and the company's own plan targets "healthy and sustainable" growth without a figure [S4][S5]. 3% keeps terminal growth under nominal GDP as the compounder card requires and is not a haircut against a company plan that carries no number.

challenges.challenge: The report prints the liquidity discount as 0.3% ('takes 0.3% off that', 'sets a 0.3% discount') and the ADTV as 'IDR20,713,317.5bn a day'. The model applies 30% (tp 2,298.98 x 0.70 = 1,609.29) and the datapack ADTV is Rp20,713,317/day. A 0.3% haircut would give ~Rp2,292, not 1,609. The same pctv unit error misprints scenario probabilities as 0.2%/0.5%/0.2% (actual 25/50/25), terminal growth as 0.0% (actual 3.0%) and TV share as 0.3% (actual 27.6%, pv_tv 32.05/EV 116.12). The single driver of a -36% SELL is therefore unreproducible from the text.
challenges.answer: Fixed every pctv unit that carried a fraction. The report now prints the discount as 30.0%, turnover as IDR20.7m a day, scenario probabilities as 25/50/25, terminal growth as 3.0% and the TV share as 36.4%, and shows the target as the weighted twelve-month value minus the discount so it is reproducible: 3,029 less 30% gives 2,120 [S0].

challenges.challenge: NWC is held at the FY2025 peak 34.7% of sales for the whole forecast and terminal, against UCID 16.5%, KINO 8.0% and MSJA 28.7%. The 9M2026 related-party receivable fell from Rp359.4bn to Rp239.2bn (-33%), which suggests collection, and the FY2026E FCFF already depends on a working-capital release. A what-if at 20% NWC lifts the DCF from Rp2,044 to ~Rp2,492 (+22%); at UCID's 16.5% it reaches ~Rp2,598, above the Rp2,560 price. The report never sensitises NWC and instead says 'the sensitivity that matters is not revenue or margin'.
challenges.answer: Normalising to a peer ratio is not supported by the latest filing: NWC at 30 September 2026 is 701.0 on LTM sales of 2,078, or 33.7%, essentially the FY2025 34.7%, because inventory of 577.4 and payables of 91.7 offset the 120.3 fall in the affiliate receivable [S5][S0]. The receivable collection is real but did not shrink working capital, so we keep the sourced ratio and instead run NWC as a scenario shock (bear +4pp, bull -4pp) and name it in section 4 as the third value driver; a leaner ratio would raise value and we say so.

challenges.challenge: The 27.0% pre-CPO gross margin is below the 9M2026 actual 28.2% (gross profit 427.31/1,512.83) and below the FY2025 underlying 26.4% ex the Rp15.6bn write-down; the CPO overlay then subtracts another 0.5-0.9pp, so FY2027E is 26.1-26.5%, ~1.7-2.1pp below the latest actual with no sourced reason for the decline. The sensitivity grid shows +/-1pp GM is worth ~Rp525/share (23% of value), so this is a rating-relevant default haircut, which the most-likely-base-case card forbids.
challenges.answer: Gross margin now starts at 27.5% before the palm link, anchored on 9M2026 gross profit of 427.3 on sales of 1,512.8 (28.2%) and the FY2025 underlying 26.4% ex the 15.563 write-down, landing at 27.0% after the CPO overlay - above the FY2025 underlying rate rather than below the latest actual [S5][S4]. The decline the red team objected to is now only in the bear, where the royalty goes to its ceiling and the write-down repeats.

challenges.challenge: The bull case only shocks revenue +3pp and GM +2pp, giving Rp2,779 - +8.5% before the 30% haircut and -24% after it. It omits the control-event upside the summary itself calls 'the clean way out': a tender/delisting at a premium to book (book Rp4,443/share, +74% vs price) with CVC, a PE owner, now controlling the Japanese parent through Kalon, and the 15 Dec EGM ahead. It also omits any cash-distribution case even though net cash is 69% of market cap. No scenario reaches the price, so the SELL cannot be falsified.
challenges.answer: The control event is now a sourced bridge item rather than prose: a tender at book (equity of 1,834.3, Rp4,463 a share) at probability 0.2 adds 182.6 to DCF equity, lifting value from below the 2,560 price to 2,745, and section 4 states the value with and without it [S5][S7]. It is kept out of the bull scenario so operating and transaction outcomes stay separable, and the bull is now labelled as an operating case.

challenges.challenge: The bear leaves out the governance levers that move minority earnings most. S4 note 33b sets the Mandom Corp royalty at 2-6% of net sales; the FY2025 charge of Rp94.711bn is 4.41% of net sales (the 5.94% in the note is 5.94% of COGS, not sales, contrary to the assumption basis). Moving to the 6% cap adds ~Rp34bn, versus FY2026E net profit of Rp11.9bn, and would wipe out the earnings base. The bear also ignores impairment of the Rp239.2bn receivable from the affiliated distributor (72% of trade receivables) and a repeat inventory write-down (Rp57.7bn FY2024, Rp15.6bn FY2025).
challenges.answer: Royalty base corrected to 4.41% of FY2025 net sales (94.711 on 2,146.553); the 5.94% in the related-party note is of COGS, and the fact label now says so [S4]. The bear carries a 2.8pp gross-margin shock that is exactly the royalty reset to the 6% ceiling (1.6pp) plus a repeat of the inventory write-down and discounting, with NWC +4pp and cash yield -0.75pp [S4][S5]. The 239.2 receivable impairment is disclosed in section 5 as the largest unmodelled downside because it fell a third in nine months, so we did not put it in the grid.

challenges.challenge: The report says the FY2025 AR shows 'the public with the small remainder' and uses a 15.1% free float. S4 shows Mandom Corp 65.23%, PT Asia Jaya Paramita 11.37%, PT Asia Paramita Indah 1.62%, Lie Harjono 0.13%, Kagami 0.01% and the public 21.64% (23.40% including the small affiliate holdings) - the public is the larger minority block, not the small remainder. The datapack's 15.13% also contradicts its own 79.276% insider figure, which implies 20.7%. The 15.1% supports the beta premium and the 'a 15.1% float cannot absorb institutional flow' sentence.
challenges.answer: Register restated from the audited AR: Mandom Corporation 65.23% (F33), PT Asia Jaya Paramita 11.37% (F34) and a public line of 23.40% (F35) of which the each-below-five-per-cent block is 21.643% (F26) [S4]. Sections 1 and 6 now carry those figures, the pack's 79.276%/15.13% pair is flagged as internally inconsistent and not used, and the beta and liquidity narrative cites the 21.6% public block.

challenges.challenge: The report uses related-party sales of Rp1,097.5bn (9M2026) as sales 'of the IDR1,512.8bn sold', but that is the gross related-party disclosure. S5's customer-concentration note puts net sales to PT Asia Paramita Indah at Rp954.9bn, 63.1% of net sales. The gross figure exceeds total domestic net sales of Rp965.2bn by Rp132bn, which is impossible as revenue. The same gross/net confusion affects the FY2025 '+30%' claim (gross +26.3%, net +31.0%) and the 'receivables (415)' in the NWC basis (actual PT Asia Paramita Indah receivable Rp239.2bn at 9M2026, Rp359.4bn at FY2025).
challenges.answer: Net sales to the affiliated distributor are now 954.877, or 63.1% of 1,512.8, from the customer-concentration note (F23); the 1,097.505 figure is relabelled as the gross Note 33 related-party disclosure, with a footnote saying it exceeds domestic net sales of 965.2 and is therefore not revenue [S5]. FY2025 growth now cites domestic +30.9% (F32) and the NWC paragraph uses the 239.2 receivable (F24) against 359.4 at December (F25).

challenges.challenge: The report asserts 'the market and the model roughly agree on the operating value'. They do not: the DCF EV is Rp116.1bn = 1.3x FY2026E EBITDA of Rp89.9bn, while the market EV is Rp323.7bn (mcap Rp1,029.5bn less net cash Rp705.8bn) = 3.6x, or Rp405bn = 4.5x on the report's own FY2026E net-debt figure. The equity values agree only because both are 69-86% cash. The 3.5x operating-value gap - not just illiquidity - is the fundamental call, and the report downplays it as 'a mild negative'.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now shows the operating comparison explicitly: DCF enterprise value of 215.5 on FY2026E EBITDA of 100.2 against the market's 4.0x on the same EBITDA, roughly twice our operating value [S0]. It states the fundamental view separately from the mandated haircut - 2,745 with the control option and 2,291 without it, versus the 2,560 price, then 2,120 after the 30% discount - and drops the claim that the market and the model agree.

challenges.challenge: The terminal value of Rp86.8bn against FY2035E EBITDA of Rp119.7bn implies a ~0.7x exit EV/EBITDA, with terminal EBIT of -Rp2.2bn. That is a liquidation-style exit, not a going-concern terminal, yet the report only says the exit multiple is 'no higher than the entry multiple' and never states it. The compounder card requires the implied exit multiple to be shown and justified; a sub-1x EBITDA perpetuity for a 3%-growth going concern needs an argument.
challenges.answer: The exit is now disclosed and defended: terminal value of 212.5 against FY2035E EBITDA of 133.1 implies about 1.6x, versus 4.0x at market, with terminal EBIT positive at 11.1 and terminal growth of 3.0% [S0]. Section 4 justifies the low exit by the thin conversion of EBITDA to free cash after capex, working capital and tax and by a terminal return below the cost of capital, rather than hiding it behind 'no higher than the entry multiple'.

challenges.challenge: The sentence 'The sensitivity that matters is not revenue or margin - it is the discount for not being able to trade' sits directly above a sensitivity table that shows the 12-month value ranging from 0 to Rp3,646 on revenue/gross-margin moves, with +/-1pp GM worth ~Rp525/share. The 30% discount is a fixed house multiplier, not a sensitivity, and the same table shows the operating assumptions carry more value uncertainty than the prose concedes.
challenges.answer: The framing now matches the table: gross margin, revenue growth and working capital are named as the value drivers, the gross-margin grid is described as ranging from close to zero to above the current price, and the 30% discount is presented as a separate mandated line, not as the dominant sensitivity; the sentence saying liquidity is the only sensitivity is deleted [S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E net profit of Rp11.9bn is entirely interest income (Rp21.5bn) offsetting an operating loss (Rp-5.4bn); the base case assumes the Rp708bn cash pile stays and earns 3.75% forever. The bear does not shock cash yield (9M2026 run-rate is already lower at Rp15.1bn on a larger balance), a special dividend, a related-party loan/advance, or an acquisition. Any deployment of the cash removes the only reason the company reports a profit.
challenges.answer: Cash yield is now a scenario driver rather than a constant: the bear cuts it 0.75pp to 3.0% and the bull raises it by the same amount, mirrored [S5][S4]. Section 5 states that any deployment or distribution changes the character of the asset, treats a distribution as part of the control-event upside, and sources the 3.75% base to the FY2025 charge and the 9M2026 3.73% run-rate (F29).

challenges.challenge: Three further internal inconsistencies: (i) post_bs_review says the 15 Dec EGM has 'no transaction on the agenda [S7][S9]', but S7 is only the EGM notice and says shareholders may propose agenda items until 16 Nov 2026 - the agenda is not fixed; (ii) 'IDR99.9bn of net profit in FY2025' (actual Rp15.3bn; 99.9 is the payout ratio); (iii) 'IDR2,918.0bn employees' (actual 2,918 employees). The 'no tender was triggered for TCID minorities' sentence is also an inference from S6's silence, not a sourced regulatory conclusion.
challenges.answer: Corrected: FY2025 net profit is now placeheld at 15.3 with 99.9% shown as the payout ratio, headcount is 2,918 without a money format, and the 'no transaction' and 'no tender' inferences are removed. The catalysts now start with the 16 November agenda-proposal window, then the 23 November invitation and 20 November record date, before the 15 December meeting [S7][S6].

missing_bull_case.note: Bull only shocks revenue +3pp and GM +2pp, capping at 2,779 (+8.5% pre-discount, -24% after the 30% haircut). The two largest upsides are named but never quantified: a control event/tender at a premium to book (book is Rp4,443/share) and NWC normalisation. Even the bull scenario cannot reach the price, so the SELL is unfalsifiable.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear omits the governance levers that actually move minority earnings: royalty to the 6%-of-net-sales cap (+~Rp34bn, vs FY2026E net profit 11.9bn), impairment of the Rp239.2bn receivable from PT Asia Paramita Indah (72% of trade receivables), a repeat inventory write-down (Rp57.7bn FY2024, Rp15.6bn FY2025), and cash extraction/cash-yield shock (FY2026E profit is entirely interest income).

assumption_realism.note: Growth of +2.0/2.5/3.0% is defensible: it is close to the arithmetic of 9M2026 men's -27.6% and ladies +22.3% at the new mix, so credit for that. But GM 27.0% pre-CPO is below the 9M2026 actual 28.2% and the FY2025 underlying 26.4% ex the write-down, and NWC is held at the FY2025 peak 34.7% of sales in perpetuity versus UCID 16.5% and KINO 8.0%. Both are unsourced caution, not the most likely path.

evidence_and_citations.note: Three load-bearing citations do not say what the report claims: the AR register (public 21.6-23.4%, not 'the small remainder'); related-party sales Rp1,097.5bn is the gross disclosure, net sales to PT Asia Paramita Indah are Rp954.9bn (63.1%); and 'no tender was triggered for TCID minorities' is inferred from S6's silence, not stated. 'Lost sales in five of the last seven years' is not in the AR's 2023-25 highlights and is uncited.

valuation_method_fit.note: 100% DCF is argued in prose but the QC WARN weights.changed is unanswered. The operating value is never shown on a comparable basis: DCF EV Rp116.1bn is 1.3x FY2026E EBITDA, versus 3.6-4.5x at market. The terminal implies a ~0.7x exit EV/EBITDA and negative terminal EBIT, which the report hides behind 'no higher than the entry multiple'. The stated WACC build (7.4% rf, 4.2% ERP, 2.5% CRP, 0.85 beta) gives 13.1%, not the 11.5% used.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose claims 'the market and the model roughly agree on the operating value' when they differ by ~3.5x (1.3x vs 4.5x EBITDA) - they agree only because both are dominated by cash. It also claims 'the sensitivity that matters is not revenue or margin' directly above a table showing 12-month value ranges 0-3,646 on revenue/GM, with +/-1pp GM worth ~Rp525/share. The SELL is a house-rule multiplier, not a fundamental conclusion.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The CPO cost link and USD/IDR are wired to the right agriculture and macro decks, the 30% liquidity discount matches the constitution's <Rp100m ADTV band, and COE sits inside the 11-13% IDR band. The NWC outlier versus peers is flagged under assumption_realism, not a deck error.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual/peers with no source: gross margin (27.0% pre-link, 26.1-26.5% effective, versus 9M2026 28.2%); NWC 34.7% held in perpetuity versus UCID 16.5%, KINO 8.0%, MSJA 28.7%; capex 3.3% below D&A 4.65% (this one is sourced to four years of below-depreciation spend and is accepted). Quantified: NWC at 20% lifts DCF from 2,044 to ~2,492; at UCID's 16.5% to ~2,598, above the current price. Shocks are mirrored in form but the bear does not touch the largest governance levers.

calibration.note: FY+1 reproduces FY2025A economics: EBITDA margin actual 4.23% vs model 4.39%, gap 0.15pp, and there are no BLOCK flags. The only flag is the unaddressed WARN weights.changed, which is a documentation gap, not a calibration failure.

signoff.notes: REDUCE is defensible. The pre-haircut twelve-month value is Rp3,029 against Rp2,560, so the call is the constitution illiquidity line, not a bearish operating view, and the report separates the two explicitly. The 30.0% discount is the correct band for ADTV Rp20.7m (below the Rp100m floor) and is consistent with KINO and MRAT at 20% for ADTV Rp133.9m and Rp230.6m. The base case reproduces the latest actual, not a haircut. The three remaining FIXes are prose-level and none misstates a printed result: section 6 still says the float matters for the beta, contradicting section 4 and the constitution; the section 4 COE build should show the 1.62% default-spread deduction (7.45 - 1.62 + 0.85 x 6.72 = 11.54%); section 3 renders fell -9.3%. Correct all three at the next routine update; they do not change the target or rating.

bias.note: Anchored, not haircut: FY2026E gross margin 27.5% pre-CPO sits between the 9M2026 actual 28.2% (F20 on F10) and the FY2025 underlying 26.4% ex the F15 write-down; FY2026E revenue -4.5% follows 9M2026 -4.3% (F10); terminal g 3.0% is below nominal GDP 8.7%. Calibration is +0.66pp EBITDA margin vs FY2025A, explained by that gross-margin anchor. Scenarios mirror revenue +/-3pp, NWC +/-4pp and cash yield +/-0.75pp at 25/50/25; the GM shocks are -2.8/+2.0, the extra bear 0.8pp being the sourced write-down repeat (F15). The 20% control-event bridge takes pre-haircut value above the price; the REDUCE is the mandated 30% liquidity discount, not an operating view. No unsourced conservatism or optimism of rating size found. Recomputations: EBITDA 90.845, net cash 705.803, revenue 2,146.553, book equity 1,834.265.

findings.finding: Section 6 says the corrected float is thin enough to matter for liquidity and for the beta used in section four, but section 4 says the float and turnover are not in the discount rate and the constitution prices illiquidity only once in the mandated discount. The engine beta is 0.85 with coe_premium 0.0, so the text describes a double count the model does not make.

Section 4 enumerates the COE build as rf 7.4% plus ERP 4.2% plus CRP 2.5% with beta 0.85, which sums to 13.1-13.5%, not the 11.5% used. The engine formula is COE = rf 7.45% minus the 1.62% Indonesia default spread plus 0.85 x (4.23% ERP + 2.46% CRP) = 11.54%; the default-spread term appears in the wacc table and assumptions coe_basis but is missing from the prose build. This is the judge FIX.
Section 3 reads FY2024 revenue fell -9.3%; the engine revenue_growth is -9.3%, so the prose sign reads as growth.

The bear gross-margin shock is -2.8pp and the bull +2.0pp, while the royalty floor is a 2.41pp benefit; the extra bear 0.8pp is the write-down repeat and the bull takes less than the full royalty reset. The asymmetry is conservative and explained in the narratives, but the method card asks for mirrored shocks or a recorded reason.
Section 3 asserts the accruals ratio is not the problem without stating the three-year ratio or the cash-conversion trend that the earnings-quality card output contract requires.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'pe': 0.3, 'div_yield': 0.1}
flags.justification: A single DCF is the right method set here: FY2026E net profit is entirely interest income on a 708 cash pile, so a P/E capitalises the cash at an operating multiple, and the 1.8% FY2026E dividend yield is that same interest income redistributed, so a yield method values the payout policy rather than the business [S4][S5]. The DCF prices the cash at face and the operations on their own cash flow.
